children: Regulators are investigating crashes that involved cars equipped with autonomous-driving products from startup Comma.ai.

The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said its investigations division identified five crashes, some of which were fatal, where vehicles with Comma.ai devices installed reportedly struck vehicles that were stopped or moving slowly in the same travel lane.

Comma.ai's devices aim to augment automated-driving capabilities in a range of car models. The devices connect to existing vehicle systems, and use cameras alongside stock vehicle sensors to provide automated control of speed and vehicle heading, with options for other features enabled by its software. Comma.ai sells its devices, and provides setup instructions, directly to consumers.

Two of the crashes identified by NHTSA resulted in a total of three deaths. Four of the five crashes contributed to non-fatal injuries, including serious injuries, to 11 other individuals, the regulator said.
A preliminary data review suggests that the Comma.ai system may not have adequately detected or responded to the in-lane vehicles, the NHTSA said.

The NHTSA said its investigation will look further into any incidents involving the Comma.ai devices and its Openpilot software system, and focus in particular on crashes involving slower or stopped vehicles or hazards in a lane.
A spokesperson for Comma.ai couldn't immediately be reached for comment.
